correctness.rationale: At an active point every neighbourhood is infinite. The sets that contain a neighbourhood modulo finite error form a proper filter by intersecting the two witnessing neighbourhoods, and contain all cofinite sets, hence form a free filter. Nonmembership of x in D_omega(A) is exactly membership of X\A in that filter. For any A, at least one of A and its complement accumulates at x, since intersecting witnesses of two failures would give a finite neighbourhood. Meet preservation makes the two alternatives mutually exclusive, giving ultrafilter dichotomy; conversely an ultrafilter makes positivity exactly filter membership, which preserves meets as well as unions, complements and bounds in the power set of S. In a decreasing countable local base at an active point, select two fresh points in each infinite member. The two disjoint selections each meet every neighbourhood infinitely and disprove the equality. If S is empty all outputs are empty. For the free-ultrafilter extension of N, all natural numbers are isolated and the ultrafilter point is active; the basic neighbourhoods are clopen and separate it from each natural number. An input accumulates at that point exactly when its trace on N is in the ultrafilter. This verifies the counterexample under the stated choice assumption, with no separation condition needed for the obstruction.
correctness.reproducibility: The frozen verify.py and VERIFICATION.md were inspected, not executed. On a finite carrier, a filter with nonempty generating kernel K has positive sets exactly those meeting K, which preserve meets exactly for singleton K. The stated 57 kernels and 36084 pair-tests are the sums of 2^n−1 and (2^n−1)4^n respectively for n=1,...,5. This finite regression cannot test nontrivial omega-accumulation in any finite space, the infinite diagonal, or existence of a free ultrafilter; these are addressed by the proof. An empty S gives the one-element codomain Boolean algebra.

evidence: The halo interpretation and its finite-join law are known. Realizing the example as the subspace of beta N consisting of N plus one free ultrafilter identifies the construction as standard.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither the abstract dichotomy nor the standard space is claimed as new. The halo law alone does not force meet preservation; the proof must identify the local cofinite-neighborhood filters, exclude every active first-countable point by disjoint infinite traces, and show that the standard ultrafilter-point topology satisfies the law on all subsets. No inspected source supplies this topological boundary.

originality.rationale: The accumulation operator, filter/grill mechanism and one-free-ultrafilter topology are standard or previously supplied. The supported distinct result is the combined all-valuations characterization for this operator with its sharp topological obstruction and simultaneous Hausdorff, countable and zero-dimensional witness. The strongest inspected same-operator comparisons study disjunction, the logic of a particular nonexample, or closure of the image family rather than this law.
residual_risks: The cited Boolean filter lemma and ultrafilter-point construction are standard. Equivalent accounts may appear in ideal topology or convergence theory; this review does not establish priority.
The identified Janković–Hamlett full text was not available for substantive comparison.

value.rationale: It gives an exact validity criterion for a natural conjunctive law of the halo operator, not merely a filter construction: local countable bases rule it out everywhere any accumulation is possible, whereas countability of the whole space plus strong separation still allows a nontrivial model. That contrast distinguishes the relevant topological hypothesis and gives an explicit test and witness.
